sources.title: New models and developer products announced at DevDay
sources.evidence: November 6, 2023 announcement introduces GPT-4 Turbo as the next generation of GPT-4, initially available as gpt-4-1106-preview with 128K context and function calling. Vision initially used the separate gpt-4-vision-preview identifier; integration into the main stable model was planned. Reopened October 27, 2026: the next-generation and performance-optimization statements provide neither a nominal count nor an explicit unchanged-parameter lineage.

sources.title: GPT-4 Turbo model documentation
sources.evidence: Current HTML and Markdown identify gpt-4-turbo with the gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 snapshot, 128,000-token context, 4,096-token maximum output, text and image input, text output and supported function calling. The page marks the model shut down. It does not disclose parameter counts, exact architecture or a dedicated reasoning mode. The exact model documentation was independently searched and fetched again on October 27, 2026; neither total nor active parameters is listed.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog, April 9, 2024
sources.evidence: The April 9, 2024 entry records general availability of GPT-4 Turbo with Vision in the API, distinguishing the stable model from the November 2023 previews.

sources.title: Deprecations: legacy GPT model snapshots
sources.evidence: The April 22, 2026 notice specifies October 23, 2026 shutdown for gpt-4-turbo and its gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 snapshot. This documents service retirement, not a runtime test.

sources.title: Introducing gpt-oss
sources.evidence: The August 5, 2025 release identifies gpt-oss as OpenAI's first open-weight language models since GPT-2, corroborating that the intervening GPT-4 Turbo release did not distribute open weights. Its parameter table describes gpt-oss, not GPT-4 Turbo.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: The agreement effective January 1, 2026 governs developer API services, grants limited access and use rights, and reserves service intellectual property. Together with the hosted GPT-4 Turbo release, this supports a descriptive proprietary classification, not an open-weight license or a claim that these exact terms applied in 2023.

sources.title: Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders
sources.evidence: This June 2024 OpenAI interpretability paper studies GPT-4 and scaled models sharing its architecture and training setup. It never identifies GPT-4 Turbo. Its 16-million latent count is for an auxiliary sparse autoencoder, not production-model parameters; generic GPT-4 evidence is not transferred to the Turbo alias. Reopened the original full HTML and freshly cached full text on October 27, 2026; no exact Turbo identification or count was found.

sources.title: GPT-4o System Card
sources.evidence: This later first-party model card explicitly compares GPT-4o performance with GPT-4 Turbo, but does not disclose GPT-4 Turbo total or active parameters or its architecture. Its GPT-4o training discussion and other model comparison rows do not establish Turbo specifications. Reopened the full card and freshly cached PDF text on October 27, 2026; the text/code performance comparison and GPT-4T clinical benchmark table do not supply either count.

sources.title: DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence
sources.evidence: Freshly opened original full HTML/PDF on October 27, 2026 and cross-checked the developer repository. Table 2 defines #TP as total parameters and #AP as active parameters. Tables 3 and 4 explicitly identify GPT-4-Turbo-0409 and give a dash in both columns; later code-repair and mathematics tables do the same. These original benchmark comparisons therefore supply no nominal Turbo count, despite reporting both counts for open models.

sources.title: Incompressible Knowledge Probes: Estimating Black-Box LLM Parameter Counts via Factual Capacity (v2)
sources.evidence: Freshly opened original July 2026 revision and downloaded/read its full PDF on October 27, 2026. Table 15 identifies gpt-4-turbo but leaves Params, IKP Pred. and Arch as dashes. Section 6.3 and Table 2 describe proprietary-model outputs as calibrated effective knowledge capacity in open-model-equivalent parameters with wide prediction bands, not measured or disclosed production counts. Neither a supported nominal total nor an activated-parameter specification for Turbo is established.

sources.title: EcoLogits proprietary-model estimation methodology
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27, 2026. The original methodology explicitly estimates GPT-4-Turbo at 880B total and 88B–264B active by assuming it is a distilled, half-size GPT-4 based on output-token prices; its GPT-4 premise comes from leaked architecture data. These are environmental-modeling assumptions, not OpenAI disclosures or an independently established nominal active-count convention, so none is adopted.

name.note: Official product and alias name; not GPT-4, GPT-4o or the separate Turbo preview alias.

developer.note: OpenAI publishes the launch and model documentation.

family.note: The launch and exact model documentation identify Turbo as the next generation of GPT-4; normalize to the GPT-4 family.

release_date.note: Earliest public release of the named GPT-4 Turbo model was the November 6, 2023 preview. This date does not claim that the final unversioned stable alias or April 2024 snapshot existed then; stable vision availability began April 9, 2024.

open_weights.note: Released through the paid hosted API, without downloadable weights; the later first-open-weights-since-GPT-2 statement corroborates closed release status.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted proprietary model under API service terms, not an SPDX identifier or a downloadable-weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 search and original-source reinspection found no developer nominal total or explicit unchanged-count lineage for exact GPT-4 Turbo. DeepSeek-Coder-V2 Tables 3/4 leave GPT-4-Turbo-0409 total parameters blank; the July 2026 IKP Table 15 also leaves the exact model count blank. Pricing-based distillation assumptions and calibrated effective-knowledge estimates are not published model specifications. Generic GPT-4 and auxiliary autoencoder counts are not transferred.

active_parameters_b.note: Independently rechecked active counts in official sources and later original research comparisons. DeepSeek-Coder-V2 explicitly labels #AP as active parameters but leaves the exact GPT-4-Turbo-0409 row blank. No later supported nominal activated count was found; EcoLogits derives its active range from assumed architecture and pricing, while IKP calibrates effective knowledge capacity. No dense-equals-total or family-count inference is used.

architecture.note: Exact-Turbo first-party searches and later training/interpretability sources did not establish even a directly bound Transformer label. The SAE paper names GPT-4 without specifying Turbo; its architecture is not transferred. Dense versus MoE remains unknown.

context_window.note: The exact alias documentation explicitly states 128,000 tokens, not the binary expansion 131,072. This is the last-documented stable snapshot context; 4,096 is its separate output limit.

modalities.note: Last-documented April 2024 stable snapshot supports text/image input and text output. Initial November 2023 vision access used a separate preview identifier; the record is not a frozen configuration of the text-only November preview.

reasoning.note: The examined exact model specifications do not explicitly establish support or non-support for a dedicated reasoning mode. General reasoning benchmark performance cannot establish this field, so the baseline false is cleared.

tool_call.note: Function calling is explicitly supported by the exact stable alias documentation, and was announced for the original text Turbo preview. This does not assert identical capabilities for the separate initial vision preview.

description.value: GPT-4 model with a 128,000-token context window; its April 2024 stable snapshot accepts text and images, generates text, and supports function calling.
description.note: Replace the unsupported compact/low-latency/high-volume characterization with documented capabilities and identify the stable snapshot scope.

patch.description: GPT-4 model with a 128,000-token context window; its April 2024 stable snapshot accepts text and images, generates text, and supports function calling.

patch.notes: The release date is the November 6, 2023 Turbo preview; listed capabilities describe the stable gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 snapshot with vision. OpenAI documents its October 23, 2026 API shutdown. Total and active parameters remain undisclosed: exact-model research comparison tables supply neither count. Pricing-based and effective-knowledge estimates are not model specifications. Architecture and dedicated reasoning-mode support remain unverified.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit reopened the exact OpenAI model documentation, DevDay announcement, sparse-autoencoder research and GPT-4o card, then checked original DeepSeek-Coder-V2 comparisons and July 2026 IKP research. Both total and active counts remain undisclosed; exact Turbo rows provide no count, and pricing-derived or effective-knowledge estimates do not establish nominal specifications. Added explicit null parameter patches and source evidence. Preserved all twelve other field assessments.
